result.summary: This PR fixes a logic bug in AddrManImpl::AddSingle() where the nTime comparison used to detect duplicate address announcements did not account for the 2-hour time penalty already applied when the entry was first stored. As a result, a single self-announcement relayed via gossip from multiple peers could incorrectly increase an address's multiplicity (RefCount) in the new table, up to 8x. The fix applies the same time penalty in the comparison, matching the existing nTime update check just above it, and adds a test covering the previously broken behavior.
result.problem: Node operators and the address manager's internal statistics are affected: gossip-relayed address announcements from multiple peers could inflate an address's apparent multiplicity in the new table, distorting address selection probabilities even though it originated from a single real announcement. The author notes this does not open a new adversarial vector since peers can already achieve similar inflation by varying nTime deliberately.
